AAS 2025 Prizes
02/13/2025
by Asia Now
Annual Conference , 2025 Annual Conference , 2025 Book Prizes , Announcement
The AAS is pleased to announce the winners of this year’s prize competitions and offer congratulations to all honorees. Many Thanks to everyone who joined us at the AAS2025 Awards Ceremony in Columbus!
Photos from the event are now available on the AAS official Flickr page.
Awards Ceremony Photos
Photo: AAS President Hyaeweol Choi presents the 2025 Distinguished Contributions to Asian Studies Award to Bruce Cumings.
Prizes for Books and Scholarship
East and Inner Asia Council
Joseph Levenson Prize (China, pre-1900)
Xin Wen , The King’s Road: Diplomacy and the Remaking of the Silk Road (Princeton University Press)
Honorable mention: Yiwen Li , Networks of Faith and Profit: Monks, Merchants, and Exchanges between China and Japan, 839–1403 CE (Cambridge University Press)
Joseph Levenson Prize (China, post-1900)
Xiaofei Kang, Enchanted Revolution: Ghosts, Shamans, and Gender Politics in Chinese Communist Propaganda, 1942-1953 (Oxford University Press)
Honorable Mention: Jie Li, Cinematic Guerrillas: Propaganda, Projectionists, and Audiences in Socialist China (Columbia University Press)
Bei Shan Tang Prizes (Chinese Art History)
Bei Shan Tang Monograph Prize
Jeffrey Moser , Nominal Things: Bronzes in the Making of Medieval China (University of Chicago Press)
Bei Shan Tang Catalogue Prize
Jessica Harrison-Hall and Julia Lovell , editors, China’s Hidden Century 1796–1912 (The British Museum)
Honorable mention: Wen-shing Chou and Daniel M. Greenberg , editors, C.C. Wang: Lines of Abstraction (Hirmer)
Northeast Asia Council
John Whitney Hall Prize (Japan)
Anne Allison , Being Dead Otherwise (Duke University Press)
Honorable mention: Akiko Takeyama , Involuntary Consent: The Illusion of Choice in Japan’s Adult Video Industry (Stanford University Press)
James B. Palais Prize (Korea)
Sixiang Wang , Boundless Winds of Empire: Rhetoric and Ritual in Early Choson Diplomacy with Ming China (Columbia University Press)
Honorable mention: Se-Mi Oh , City of Sediments: A History of Seoul in the Age of Colonialism (Stanford University Press)
Sumie Jones Prize for Project Leadership in Japan-centered Humanities
Eric Faden , Japanese Paper Film Project
Julie Iezzi , “Celebrating Kabuki in Hawai`i”
South Asia Council
Bernard S. Cohn Prize (First book on South Asia)
Hafsa Kanjwal, Colonizing Kashmir: State-building under Indian Occupation (Stanford University Press)
Rumya Sree Putcha, The Dancer’s Voice: Performance and Womanhood in Transnational India (Duke University Press)
Honorable mention: Kyle Jackson , The Mizo Discovery of the British Raj (Cambridge University Press)
Honorable mention: Mayur Suresh , Terror Trials: Life and Law in Delhi’s Courts (Fordham University Press)
Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy Prize (South Asia)
Adam Auerbach and Tariq Thachil , Migrants and Machine Politics: How India’s Urban Poor Seek Representation and Responsiveness (Princeton University Press)
Neeti Nair , Hurt Sentiments: Secularism and Belonging in South Asia (Harvard University Press)
Southeast Asia Council
Harry J. Benda Prize (First book on Southeast Asian Studies)
Adam Bobbette , The Pulse of the Earth: Political Geology in Java (Duke University Press)
Faizah Zakaria , The Camphor Tree and the Elephant: Religion and Ecological Change in Maritime Southeast Asia (University of Washington Press)
Honorable mention: Margaret Jack , Media Ruins: Cambodian Postwar Media Reconstruction and the Geopolitics of Technology (The MIT Press)
George McT. Kahin Prize
Christopher Goscha , The Road to Dien Bien Phu: A History of the First War for Vietnam (Princeton University Press)
A.L. Becker Southeast Asian Literature in Translation Prize
Kong Rithdee, translator of Memories of the Memories of the Black Rose Cat , by Veeraporn Nitiprapha (River Books Press)
Honorable mention: Tiffany Tsao , translator of Happy Stories, Mostly , by Norman Erikson Pasaribu (Tilted Axis Press)
Career Awards
Distinguished Contributions to Asian Studies
Bruce Cumings, University of Chicago
Citation for Exceptional Service to Asian Studies
Helena Kolenda
Graduate Student Paper Prizes
East and Inner Asia Council
Mengliu Cheng (University of Pennsylvania), “Disenchanting Foreign Knowledge: Revealing Agricultural ‘Pseudoscience’ in China, 1930s-1940s”
Ki Cora Chow (Washington University in St. Louis), “Fantasies of Nimble Fingers: Gender and Skills in Garment Women Narratives of Late Twentieth-Century Hong Kong”
Aaron Su (Princeton University), “Indigenous Feminism, Sovereignty, and the Limits of Eco-Politics: Conflicting Approaches to ‘Self-Sufficiency’ in Taiwan”
Northeast Asia Council
Narusa Yamato (Stanford University), “The Global Making of a Japanese ‘Holstein Island’: Silk, Milk, and Hachijō Island in Imperial Japan”
South Asia Council
Karthik Maini (University of Chicago), “The Career of Charisma: Marrying Kṛṣṇa and Muḥammad in Mughal South Asia”
Southeast Asia Council
Wee Yang Soh (University of Chicago), “Modeling ‘Asian Values’ on American Conservatism: The Paradox of Singapore’s Anti-Colonial Nationalism.”
